name: Humban-haltash III
summary:
Humban-haltash III or Umanaldash was the last major ruler of Elam. He played a crucial role in the politics of the region during the Neo-Assyrian Empire's expansion (700–639 BCE). Humban-haltash III's rule was marked by his efforts to maintain Elam's independence and resistance against Assyrian forces.

Humban-haltash III was defeated and captured by the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal, who incorporated Elam into the Neo-Assyrian Empire. This event had significant consequences for the region, leading to the eventual decline of Elam as a major power.

The legacy of Humban-haltash III can be seen in the cultural exchange between Elam and neighboring regions, including the adoption of Assyrian architecture and art forms. His rule also saw the continued development of trade networks and economic ties with other civilizations.

In the 7th century BCE, Humban-haltash III's defeat marked a turning point in the history of Elam, leading to its eventual absorption into the Neo-Assyrian Empire. This event has been studied by historians to understand the dynamics of imperial expansion and the impact on regional politics.

"The fall of Elam was a significant blow to our power, but we will not forget the lessons of Humban-haltash III's bravery." - Ashurbanipal, Assyrian king
